challenges.name: deploy-health-gate-quiz
challenges.title: Read the deploy that went green
challenges.description: Three statements about the deploy job that reported success while Rice Rocket's api was down. Decide whether each one is true.
hints: The runner decides pass or fail from one thing only: the exit code of the step's shell. What exit code does curl return when the server answers 502 and no `-f` flag is set?
Every step has an implicit `if: success()` unless it says otherwise. What does that do to a step placed after one that failed?
Step outputs live inside their job. Look at which map a later job reads through `needs.<job>.outputs`, and where that map is declared.

questions.question:
The deploy job checked the api after `docker compose up -d`:

```yaml
      - name: Check health
        run: curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://api.ricerocket.vn/health
```

```text
Check health
  502
  ✓ Check health (1s)
Job deploy succeeded
```

Statement: "The step passed because the runner retried the request and the 502 was transient; the api was healthy by the time the step finished."
questions.explanation: False. The runner does not retry steps, and a step passes whenever its shell exits 0. curl exits 0 on any HTTP answer, 502 included, unless it is told to treat HTTP errors as failures: `curl -fsS` (or `--fail-with-body`) exits 22 on a 4xx or 5xx, which fails the step. The log printed 502 and the step still went green; nothing in it shows a second request. The misconception is that a step fails when its output looks bad: only the exit code counts.

questions.question:
After the health step failed, the rollback step did not run:

```yaml
      - name: Health gate
        run: node deploy/gate.js
      - name: Roll back
        run: ssh deploy@vps 'cd /srv/rice-rocket && TAG=1.3.2 docker compose up -d'
```

```text
X Health gate
  Error: Process completed with exit code 1.
- Roll back   (skipped)
```

Statement: "A runner error skipped the rollback step; re-running the failed job will run it."
questions.explanation: False. Every step without an `if:` runs as `if: success()`, so once Health gate fails every later plain step is skipped: that is the documented behavior, not a runner error, and a re-run skips it again. A cleanup step that must run after a failure needs `if: failure()` (or `always()` for both cases). Better still, keep the rollback inside the gate script, where it runs right after the failed check and the step still exits non-zero.

questions.question:
The deploy job writes the version it shipped, and a later job posts it to the team chat:

```yaml
jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - id: gate
        run: echo "version=1.4.0" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  announce:
    needs: deploy
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - run: echo "Shipped ${{ needs.deploy.outputs.version }}"
```

```text
announce  Run echo "Shipped "
  Shipped
```

Statement: "`needs.deploy.outputs` holds only what the deploy job declares in its own `outputs:` map, so the job needs `outputs: { version: ${{ steps.gate.outputs.version }} }`."
questions.explanation: True. A step output (`$GITHUB_OUTPUT`) is visible to later steps of the same job as `steps.gate.outputs.version`. Other jobs see only the job-level `outputs:` map, which maps names to step outputs; without it `needs.deploy.outputs.version` is an empty string, and the expression does not fail, so the bug shows up only as a blank message.

challenges.name: deploy-health-gate
challenges.title: Gate the deploy on health, roll back on failure
challenges.description: Rice Rocket's deploy job ran `docker compose up -d` over SSH and went green at once, while image 1.4.0 crash-looped for ten minutes. The new step runs `deploy/gate.js` on the VPS. The editor holds the module with its key blocks missing, each marked by a `// [ ]` line; some pieces are wrong on purpose. `gateDeploy({ release, previous, policy }, io)` must: roll `release` out; ask `io.health()` once per `policy.intervalMs` until `policy.okInARow` answers in a row have status 200 and report `version === release`, or until `policy.timeoutMs` has passed (a thrown error is a failed check and breaks the streak; do not sleep after the last good answer); when healthy, write the outputs `deployed=<release>` and `rolled_back=false`, add a summary line and return `{ status: "deployed", version: release, checks, exitCode: 0 }`; otherwise roll `previous` back out, write `deployed=<previous>` and `rolled_back=true`, add a summary line and return `{ status: "rolled_back", version: previous, checks, exitCode: 1 }`. On a first deploy (`previous` is null) there is nothing to restore: write `rolled_back=false` and a summary line, and return `{ status: "failed", version: release, checks, exitCode: 1 }`. Run grades it against a scripted server and a fake clock.
hints: Walk through one failing deploy on paper: which answers come back from the server while the old container stops and the new one crash-loops, and which of them may count toward the streak?

Look at the loop: one piece asks for health and turns a thrown error into a failed check, the next one updates `streak`. After the loop, the order is: healthy, then no previous version, then roll back.

A queue consumer that waits for 5 good batches in a row from worker version 2.0: `if (batch && batch.ok && batch.workerVersion === "2.0") good++; else good = 0;`, and when time runs out it calls `scale("1.9")`, logs the reason and returns `{ exitCode: 1 }` so the job fails.

tests.name: Ships 1.4.0 after three good answers in a row from the new version
Crash loop: rolls back to 1.3.2 at the deadline and fails the step
The old container answering 200 does not count as the new version
A flapping container never reaches three good answers in a row
First deploy without a previous version fails and rolls nothing back
Stops as soon as the streak is complete, without sleeping again
